# Autonomous-agent workflows with CTT

[Documentation map](index.md) · [Quickstart](../README.md#quickstart-find-the-next-agent-tasks) · [API reference](reference.md)

Use CTT when agents or tools perform work with dependencies: research before implementation, independent specialist tasks in parallel, verification after several branches, or review after an entire composite completes. CTT supplies graph discovery, dependency readiness, lifecycle transitions, and inspection. Your coordinator supplies the workflow and executes it.

## On this page

- [Explore context and references](#explore-context-and-references)
- [Reuse workflow fragments](#reuse-workflow-fragments)
- [Choose an execution model](#choose-an-execution-model)
- [Discover the graph](#discover-the-graph)
- [Work dependencies and completion joins](#work-dependencies-and-completion-joins)
- [Accept results and resume](#accept-results-and-resume)
- [Persist facts and reconstruct](#persist-facts-and-reconstruct)
- [Retries, human waits, and graph revisions](#retries-human-waits-and-graph-revisions)
- [Troubleshoot a workflow](#troubleshoot-a-workflow)

## Explore context and references

Choose `GraphWalk` / `AsyncGraphWalk` to gather context, follow code references or collect provenance from cyclic/shared information graphs. Choose DAG traversal when relationships mean work/completion prerequisites. A walking edge has caller-defined meaning and supplies no dispatch readiness. A found isolated root still produces a vertex; parallel and back edges remain observable in the same walk. See the [five-vertex/six-relationship context example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/graph-walk-context-example.ts) and [exact walking contracts](reference.md#general-graph-walking).

For a finite in-memory catalog, use `materializeWalkSourceFromRecords(items, { id, outgoing, roots })`; its async counterpart materializes async inputs once and returns a synchronous source. For lazy retrieval, supply `source.roots()` and `source.outgoing(vertex)` with an explicit hydration mode. Use `hydration: 'resolver'` with required `resolveVertex(id)` and mixed `{ vertexId }` / `{ vertexId, resolution }` targets. Use `hydration: 'inlineOrCached'` without a resolver and tagged `{ kind: 'inline', vertexId, resolution }` / `{ kind: 'cached', vertexId }` targets; cached targets require a prior admitted resolution, including for self/backedges. Walking materializers declare resolver mode. Reuse `GraphWalkRecordSelectors` / `AsyncGraphWalkRecordSelectors` for catalogs; `GraphWalkCatalogLink` has readonly `to`/`data` fields, separate from lazy target wrappers. `materializeWalkSourceFromDagDefinition(definition, { relations })` explicitly projects selected declaration links without DAG execution validation. Do not pass a `DagDiscoverySource` / `TreeSource` directly; their source context and omission contracts differ.

Use phase-keyed vertex and edge visitors to collect typed endpoint data in one session. Use `iterateEvents({ emitEvents: [...] })` for pull integration; explicit selections narrow the delivered event union, while callbacks are independently controlled by `visitorPhases`. `walkGraph(options)` / `await walkGraphAsync(options)` are one-shot helpers returning the runner. Source callbacks and visitors execute serially, including async walking; no concurrency setting is accepted. The [reference example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/graph-walk-references-example.ts) shows callbacks, async iteration, endpoint discriminants, common inspection and wrappers that preserve each family's phase type.

Default `revisit: 'once'` collects each vertex and every followed relationship. Select `simplePaths` for prefixes without repeated vertices, or `walks` for repeated routes; both require a depth or candidate-read-attempt bound. Always carry `runner.summary().outcome` into a host result so `limited` cannot be mistaken for completeness. Paths include every prefix; parallel relationships can produce identical vertex sequences with distinct edge indices. DFS depth bounds apply to its first route; BFS finds shortest discovery depths. See the [bounded provenance example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/graph-walk-paths-example.ts).

The host owns authorization, retrieval policy, stable IDs, relationship meaning, retries, freshness, timeouts, persistence and any agent/model invocation. The first admitted resolution for an ID wins, including omission; a fresh runner is required to observe replacement data. Walking does not retry omissions or certify a remote transactional snapshot. A budget bounds candidate read attempts, admitted targets and depth, not host callback duration or tokens. Consumer iterator `return()`/loop break pauses and retains resources for continuation; terminal runner `close()` disposes them after execution ownership has been released. Active terminal close rejects: first return the iterator or request and await pause. Iterator return/pause and async cleanup require pending host work to settle and do not cancel promises. A failed runner retains its exact error; closing it rethrows that same error without repeating cleanup. Retain/dispose paused runners deliberately; there is no durable walking checkpoint or built-in network/LLM integration.

## Reuse workflow fragments

Capture a discovered topology through `prepared.definition`, or author materialized source facts with `defineDag` and validate them with `prepareDagDefinition`. `defineDagFragment(definition, ports)` names live local boundary vertices. Keep each fragment closed over its live and known omitted identities; provide all cross-fragment dependencies when composing.

Instantiate a template with `instantiateDagFragment(fragment, { mapId })`, giving each local identity a host-selected global ID. Mapping runs once per live/omitted identity and supports object IDs. Then `composeDag(instances, { dependencies, children })` concatenates ordered entries and validates the entire graph. Choose `milestone: 'work'` to wait for accepted initial work or `'subgraphCompletion'` to wait for the full retained subgraph. Structural child links and execution waits are separate options.

Invalid ports, identity collisions and nonexistent wire endpoints throw `TypeError`; cycles between valid endpoints return invalid issues. Only a valid result exposes a prepared DAG. Create independent runners or sessions from that result, selecting accepted completion facts explicitly for each run. Templates, agent roles, claims and business outcomes remain host data and policy. See the [fragment contract](reference.md#dag-fragments-and-composition) and [runnable example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-fragments-example.ts).

## Choose an execution model

| Model                    | How it works                                                                                                                                                                | Appropriate when                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Host-controlled frontier | Use a prepared DAG's `createWorkSession()`, then `advance()` and dispatch its frontier tickets; custom runners can use `createDagWorkSession` / `createAsyncDagWorkSession` | Agents run externally, work needs claims/approval, or state must survive process loss |
| Work inside visitors     | Use `AsyncDagTraversal` and await work in `ON_WORK_READY` visitors; normal chain completion releases dependents                                                             | One process owns execution and immediate callback failure should fail traversal       |

Start with the host-controlled model for a durable agent coordinator. For in-memory collections, use `materializeDagInputFromRecords` → `prepareDag` → `dag.createWorkSession({ completedWork })`. Use `await prepareDagAsync(...)` for async source discovery and `await dag.createAsyncWorkSession(...)` for an async session. `DagTraversal` is sufficient when graph facts are already in memory; use `AsyncDagTraversal` for asynchronous adapters. The host can run asynchronous agents independently of which runner it uses.

With visitor execution, `concurrency` bounds invoked callbacks, including adapters and visitors. It does not bound externally dispatched agents after external deferral, enforce a token budget, or provide distributed claims. A returned/awaited callback must represent completion of its work: launching a background job and returning immediately releases its dependents too early.

A host-controlled tick follows this sequence:

```text
load graph revision + accepted facts
              ↓
materialize source → prepare reusable definition → create session → advance
              ↓
read frontier tickets → filter claims/waits → rank candidates → claim and dispatch agents
              ↓
validate result + attempt/revision → durably accept completion
              ↓
complete retained ticket + advance again, or reconstruct next tick
```

The same vertex can remain in `readyOrDeferredIds` while an external agent is running. CTT's `activeVisitorVertexIds` tracks its own visitor chains, not the host's external attempts. Always overlay host claims, capacity, and waits before dispatch.

## Discover the graph

CTT traverses the graph your adapter provides; it does not generate a plan from a goal or work-item type. A host's `planDag` can select a type-specific template or generate and validate a revision, then adapt its nodes to CTT. `planDag` is a host function, not a CTT API. Hints describe how to discover that plan.

| Concept                          | CTT representation                                                 | Host responsibility                                                |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Stable work identity             | `vertexId`                                                         | Choose IDs that can be reconstructed and matched to accepted facts |
| Opaque task data                 | `vertexContent.$data`                                              | Agent role, prompt/artifact references, policy and metadata        |
| Discovery and structure          | `resolveRoot()`, `resolveChild(hint)`, `vertexContent.$childHints` | Supply the complete intended catalog and structural relationships  |
| Initial-work dependency          | `dependsOnWork`                                                    | Declare which work must be accepted first                          |
| Structural-completion dependency | `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`                                      | Declare which composite must finish before work begins             |
| Missing prerequisite lookup      | Optional `resolvePrerequisite(id)`                                 | Fetch graph facts from a catalog/service                           |

For a known catalog, use `materializeDagInputFromRecords(items, { id, children?, dependsOnWork?, dependsOnSubgraphCompletion? })`. Every catalog item is discovered, including disconnected entries; `children` returns structural child IDs. A child ID absent from the catalog rejects immediately, while missing prerequisite IDs reach dependency validation. For nested records, `materializeDagInputFromRoots(roots, selectors)` expands `children(item)` records iteratively and shares repeated references. Different forest records with the same ID reject; `materializeDagInputFromRecords` rejects any duplicate ID. Async variants accept iterable/async-iterable inputs and value-or-promise selectors, then return the same input envelope containing a synchronous discovery source.

Both adapters return `MaterializedDagInput` envelopes containing `traversableGraph` and `syntheticRoot: true`; pass or spread both fields together. `DagDiscoverySource` names the actual discovery protocol, while walking materializers return actual `GraphWalkSource` protocols. Both DAG adapters copy membership and edge lists once. Item data and IDs retain shallow identity: editing an item field remains visible, but editing its original edge array does not change captured topology. The hidden synthetic holder never appears in public vertices, callbacks, or events. For custom adapters, the equivalent catalog pattern uses `syntheticRoot: true`, lists every item in its `$childHints`, and declares explicit `dependsOnWork` lists. Discovery cannot detect work omitted from the supplied domain.

Call `prepareDag(source)` or `await prepareDagAsync(source)` to discover and validate once. A valid result exposes `dag.vertices` and factories for independent runners or sessions; an invalid result exposes an `issues` array. Source errors retain their exact thrown values, including a source-thrown `DagTraversalStallError`. Structural child cycles throw `DagDiscoveryCycleError` with an identity-preserving closed `vertexIds` witness; malformed-source errors also throw. Only engine dependency validation failures become `{ kind: 'invalid', issues: [{ kind: 'milestone', diagnostics }] }`, using the same result shape as definition preparation, composition and revision.

A prepared definition owns copied topology and detached readonly vertex descriptions. Each new session gets independent progress, accepted seeds, references, and settlement generations without calling the original adapter again. Replay hints are normalized to IDs; original opaque discovery hints are not retained. Preparation can perform source I/O, so business work belongs in host execution or visitors. See the [prepared definition contract](reference.md#reusable-prepared-dags).

Discovery and execution dependencies are distinct. Graph sources default to `omittedWorkDependencies: 'none'`: omitting `dependsOnWork` means no work prerequisites. Declare explicit lists (including `[]`), or set `omittedWorkDependencies: 'discoveryParentWork'` to inherit the discovery parent's W when the list is omitted. Ordinary roots honor W by default; `rootWorkDependencies: 'ignore'` suppresses root W only, never C. Children of a synthetic root have no implicit dependency on the holder. See [discovery versus execution](reference.md#discovery-and-execution-as-separate-phases).

A prerequisite ID alone does not make a vertex discoverable. Include it through hints/catalog entries or supply `resolvePrerequisite`. That hook may find further prerequisites transitively; concurrent demand is coalesced. Return `{ kind: 'found', vertex: { vertexId, vertexContent: { $data, $childHints }, dependsOnWork } }` for content, `{ kind: 'missing' }` for not found, or `{ kind: 'omitted', satisfiesDependencies: true }` for intentional omission. Omission deliberately omits the vertex and satisfies its dependencies, so it is not a representation of a failed agent or a temporary service outage. Let adapter errors propagate as appropriate. See [lookup and identity rules](reference.md#discovery-and-completed-work).

Choose discovery and dispatch surfaces by the lifetime you need:

| Need                                             | Surface                                                                                      | Execution boundary                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Reuse validated topology across independent runs | `prepareDag(source)` / `prepareDagAsync(source)`                                             | Discover and validate once; create fresh runners or sessions afterward.                                                                       |
| Preview one fresh runner before work             | `runner.prepare()` / `await runner.prepare()`                                                | Discover and validate without visitors or dispatch generations; `run()` adopts that discovery.                                                |
| Discover fully, then execute in one operation    | Runner with `discovery: 'eager'`, then `run()`                                               | Validation precedes callbacks, but execution begins in the same call.                                                                         |
| Dispatch host work                               | Session `advance()` frontier tickets, or runner `summary().awaitingSettlement` after `run()` | Use external settlement; apply host claims and capacity. `readyOrDeferredIds` is observational dependency eligibility, not a dispatch ticket. |

For a preview before dispatch, call `runner.prepare()` (await it on `AsyncDagTraversal`). It eagerly discovers the closure exposed by roots, hints and prerequisite lookup and validates the combined W/C graph, without visitors, execution events, new real-vertex completion, or deferred generations. Accepted `completedWork` seeds remain W facts. Inspect the graph at `HALTED` / `prepared`, then call `run()` to admit work without replaying discovery. Repeated preparation before execution is idempotent. This requires a fresh tree-source or graph-source runner without injected state/containers, even empty injected objects; invalid preparation requests reject recoverably. Once preparation begins, summaries report effective eager mode and eager topology freezing applies. After execution starts, preparation rejects.

Preparation can perform adapter I/O: keep business execution in the host or visitors. During async preparation, `requestPause()` stops future admissions but waits for admitted discovery callbacks to settle; callbacks are not canceled. The operation acknowledges `paused`; another `prepare()` continues it, or `run()` adopts discovery and executes. Failed preparation preserves the exact error. Empty and omitted-root previews still stop `prepared`.

Lazy execution remains available without preparation and may expose partially discovered views and summaries. `summary()` is observational and never fetches vertices. Use `DagTraversal<Workflow, Workflow, TaskId>` and `DagDiscoverySource<Workflow, Workflow, TaskId>` to carry host IDs through sources, summaries and settlement independently of data/hints. Every typed live result supplies an own `vertexId`; materialize class getters as own fields. See [identity migration](migration-uniform-api.md#caller-specified-graph-identity-types).

## Work dependencies and completion joins

| Declaration                                       | Releases the dependent after…                                                                   | Example                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `dependsOnWork: ['research']`                     | Research's initial work completes (W)                                                           | Implementation can start from accepted research              |
| `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion: ['implementation']` | Implementation's committed completion transition (C), including discovery and retained children | Review waits for implementation and all its component tasks  |
| Both lists                                        | Every declared W and C prerequisite is satisfied                                                | Review waits for a composite and a separate test-plan result |

Use work dependencies for flat agent tasks. Use completion dependencies when structural children are meaningful parts of a composite. Seeds in `completedWork` satisfy W only; children and completion visitors still have to complete before C is released.

Avoid making a child wait on its own ancestor's C when that ancestor must wait for the child to complete. CTT validates combined milestone cycles; seeding W does not make an invalid graph valid. Completion prerequisites add C gates independently of the declared W lists and the optional parent-inheritance policy. The [completion example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-completion-dependencies-example.ts) demonstrates a valid sibling join.

## Accept results and resume

Event streams filter at delivery across tree, DAG and walking runners. A new iterator lease applies its `emitEvents` selection to buffered observations and deferred settlement events. Selection never replays work or callbacks; `visitorPhases` retains independent admission snapshots. For example, resume with `emitEvents: ['subgraphCompleted']` to consume completion observations while suppressing pending work observations. See the [delivery example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/event-delivery-selection-example.ts).

Start from the [quickstart](../README.md#quickstart-find-the-next-agent-tasks). To advance its session after the host accepts `testPlan`, dispatch from the `advance()` frontier. This continuation assumes the quickstart's `session` and `accepted` values:

```ts
const pending = session.advance();
if (pending.kind === 'awaitingSettlement') {
  const ticket = pending.workTickets.find(
    (work) => work.vertexId === 'testPlan',
  )!;
  // Retain the ticket before dispatch; validate revision/attempt on the result.
  accepted.add(ticket.vertexId); // In-memory simulation of durable acceptance.
  session.completeWork(ticket);
  const next = session.advance();
  if (next.kind === 'awaitingSettlement') {
    console.log(next.workTickets.map((work) => work.vertexId)); // ['review']
  }
}
```

`advance()` drains execution and returns `awaitingSettlement` with readonly tickets, `paused`, or `finished`; async sessions return a promise. `completeWork(ticket)` and `failTraversal(ticket, error)` are synchronous. The first accepted report returns `{ kind: 'accepted' }`; the identical report returns `{ kind: 'alreadyAccepted' }`. A failure fails the whole runner and the next advance throws the exact error. Conflicting reports, copied/forged tickets, and tickets from another facade or session reject. Repeated observations of the same deferred work stay usable. Follow completion with advance to observe new work. Use `session.inspectMilestones().explain({ vertexId, milestone: 'work' })` to explain blockers without advancing, and `session.inspect()` for lifecycle state. `failTraversal` is the sole fatal settlement method.

Tickets expose only `vertexId`; their provenance and generation are private. They are local capabilities: serializing or copying a ticket does not preserve settlement authority. Filter each frontier through host claims, waits, and capacity. A ticket is not a distributed lease or persistent attempt ID. Use `summary()` for work progress/frontier, `inspectMilestones()` for dependency blockers, and `inspect()` for execution/iterator state. All three observe without advancing. `requestPause()` delegates cooperative pause to the runner.

For existing custom-source runners, set `workCompletion: 'externalSettlement'` and wrap with `createDagWorkSession(runner)` or `createAsyncDagWorkSession(runner)`. Wrapping runs no callbacks and acquires no separate execution owner; direct runner access remains available. The lower-level guarded frontier and settlement contract also remains available.

For an async runner, await `runner.run()`. `settle()` itself is synchronous. A settlement wakes an active async consumer; after idle settlement, resume explicitly. Only one iterator may own a runner at a time. All runners expose `requestPause(): boolean`: true records a new request only while RUNNING, rather than acknowledging a halt. The active owner drains admitted chains to `HALTED` / `paused` without cancellation; a suspended iterator may need `next()` or `return()` to drive that boundary. Resume the same runner without replaying committed work.

Dispatch from `summary().awaitingSettlement`: each readonly record atomically contains `{ vertexId, generation }`. It includes exactly live deferred work without an accepted outcome, in discovery order; queued-only, completed and deleted vertices are absent. Arrays and records are detached, retaining opaque ID identity. Filter this snapshot through host claims and capacity. DAG event `kind: 'workCompleted'` emits after committed W, including settlement; `kind: 'subgraphCompleted'` emits after committed C. Select these kinds with `emitEvents`; select readiness callbacks separately with `visitorPhases`. Committed events have no callback `phase` field. Seeded work emits no synthetic work event. `ON_WORK_READY` visitors remain pre-work. Completion events are not dispatch signals. Alternatively, an actual enabled `ON_WORK_READY` callback can dispatch before the external policy defers its chain. All callback commands commit before normal external deferral. `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` remains automatic once W, discovery, children, and C prerequisites permit it.

Capture the generation belonging to the deferred work you dispatched. It is a local guard, not a durable attempt ID, distributed lease, or authentication token. The host must separately reject stale revisions, stale attempts, duplicate result delivery, and lost claims before accepting a result. An identical accepted settlement returns `false`; invalid, conflicting, or cross-runner settlement throws.

`{ kind: 'workCompleted' }` means the work is complete for dependency traversal. An accepted review rejection can still complete a review vertex if host policy says the review work is done. `{ kind: 'traversalFailed', error }` fails the whole runner and preserves the exact thrown value; it is not a retry request or a business outcome field. The progress state `completed` means traversal work completion.

## Persist facts and reconstruct

CTT does not prescribe a storage engine or ship a persistence adapter. Define storage interfaces in your host and implement them with SQLite, PostgreSQL, a service, or another provider. Provider interchangeability must preserve the host's claim and result-acceptance guarantees, not just CRUD method names.

| Persist in the host                                                          | Purpose                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Graph revision, stable IDs, task definitions, W/C declarations and structure | Reconstruct the intended graph and associate results with the correct revision |
| Accepted outcomes and artifact references                                    | Decide which work is complete for traversal and supply downstream inputs       |
| Attempts, claims/leases, wait state, retry decisions and deduplication keys  | Prevent readiness from dispatching duplicate or ineligible work                |
| Accepted completion facts for the revision                                   | Supply `completedWork` to a new runner                                         |

Keep prepared definitions, runners, tickets, vertex references, generation symbols, pending promises, and lookup handles in memory. A serialized summary is useful for presentation, but is not a runner checkpoint. CTT allows arbitrary SameValueZero IDs; durable hosts should choose their own stable serializable ID convention, such as strings.

On startup or each reconciliation tick:

1. Load a consistent graph revision and its host-accepted facts.
2. Prepare the full graph revision (plus lookup if required); reuse its in-memory definition while that revision remains valid.
3. Create a fresh session with `completedWork` and call `advance()`.
4. Filter frontier tickets using persisted claims, waits, retries, and host capacity.
5. Claim and dispatch selected work. Validate incoming results and durably record accepted completion before completing a retained ticket.

This ordering lets a crash after acceptance but before settlement recover by reconstruction. A crash during an external side effect still needs host idempotency, reconciliation, or compensation; CTT does not provide exactly-once external execution. Transactional claim/acceptance, compare-and-set revisions, and dispatch outboxes are host design choices, not built-in CTT guarantees.

The [reconciliation example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-reconciliation-example.ts) verifies that reconstructing from accepted facts yields the same ready IDs as advancing a retained runner. It uses an in-memory set to illustrate the contract, not a durable storage implementation.

## Retries, human waits, and graph revisions

A revision returns invalid issues or a fresh `{ dag, changes }`; the original prepared value and its sessions remain usable. Removing a vertex leaves its references and descendants in place, so repair those references explicitly in the same batch. Data comparisons in `changes` are shallow and cannot determine whether a previously accepted artifact remains useful.

Keep host revision/attempt checks when results arrive. A ticket issued before revision throws in the new session and can still settle its original work. An admitted old async callback continues in its original runner; revision does not cancel it. Supply `completedWork` explicitly to the new session only for facts independently accepted for its definition. See [validated revision contracts](reference.md#validated-dag-revisions) and the [executable revision example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-revision-example.ts).

- **Agent retry:** retain the task as incomplete; record the failed attempt and retry policy in the host. Do not send fatal `kind: 'traversalFailed'` unless you intend to fail the runner. Deferral must be the only command in its result; mixed results are rejected before any commands apply.
- **Human input or approval:** keep the task deferred and record a host wait. Exclude it from dispatch until the response is accepted; readiness alone will keep listing it.
- **New plan or graph revision:** use `reviseDag(prepared, operations)` to validate an atomic batch of full declaration edits, then start a session from the valid result. Carry completion facts forward only when the host validates their meaning for the new revision. Do not seed every historic success blindly.
- **Cancellation or timeout:** cancel host executor work separately. Halting CTT does not cancel already-started callbacks or remote agents. Async close may wait for a pending callback.
- **Completion side effects:** prefer durable result acceptance in the host. Reconstruction can invoke completion visitors again even when initial work was seeded; make any external effects idempotent.

## Troubleshoot a workflow

| Symptom                                              | Check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Work completed without an agent running              | Check `workCompletion: 'externalSettlement'`; the default `afterWorkReadyChain` completes W on normal callback-chain return. Seeds also mark W complete                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| The same agent task dispatches again                 | Host claim/attempt state must filter `readyOrDeferredIds`; deferral intentionally leaves work ready                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Ready work seems absent                              | Run discovery first; inspect discovery completeness, seed IDs, and unmet W/C dependencies                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Missing prerequisite or cycle                        | Inspect the `milestone` issue in `invalid.issues` from source preparation or `DagTraversalStallError` from direct execution for W/C constraints. For engine-detected structural cycles, `prepareDag`/`prepareDagAsync` return `invalid` with a `discoveryCycle` issue containing the ordered closed witness; direct runners throw `DagDiscoveryCycleError`. Collection adapters reject absent child IDs with `TypeError`. Authored definitions report `invalid.issues`; exact source/caller-thrown values propagate unchanged. Check catalog coverage, lookup results and structural edges |
| A seeded composite still blocks review               | Seeds complete W, not C; its retained children and completion transition must finish                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| A retry aborts everything                            | `settle(..., { kind: 'traversalFailed', error }, ...)` is fatal; keep retryable work incomplete in host policy                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Settlement fails after restart                       | Generations are runner-local; reconstruct from accepted facts rather than replaying an old handle                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| An external task still runs after halt               | Callback/executor cancellation belongs to the host                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| A node fetched by lookup is missing from a root walk | Resolved prerequisites may be detached; enumerate `getVertexRefs()` instead of only walking `getRoot()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Use synchronous `runner.inspectMilestones()` (also on async runners), or the equivalent `inspectDagMilestones(runner)`, when a host needs to show why a milestone is blocked or which original constraints depend on it. Capture once, then call `explain({ vertexId, milestone: 'work' | 'subgraphCompletion' })`, `prerequisitesOf(...)`, or `dependentsOf(..., { transitive: true })`. Explanations distinguish unknown/deleted identities, omitted vertices, unfinished work, incomplete local discovery and pending completion transitions. A ready or externally deferred task still has unfinished W; a seeded parent's W may be satisfied while its C waits for children. Constraint endpoints include work state and milestone satisfaction, without interpreting business outcomes.

Inspect after `prepare()` for an eager validated view, or during lazy traversal for partial facts. `discoveryComplete: false` limits the captured domain, and an unresolved endpoint is not a proven missing task. Captures stay unchanged after settlement; capture again to refresh. These queries perform no callbacks, lookup, scheduling, or ownership changes, including while an iterator or pending async callback owns the runner. Static navigation keeps original constraints after milestones complete; explanations stop at satisfied milestones. See the [query contract](reference.md#dag-dependency-queries-and-explanations) and [runnable inspection example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-inspection-example.ts).

Use `summary()` for DAG work readiness and diagnostics. Use `inspect()` for callback/iterator execution state. Inspection reports callback `phase` separately from chain `state`, `visitorIndex`, and admitted `executionOptions`; pending requests name their public callback `operation`. Graph `visitStage` records scheduling boundaries and cannot establish active callbacks or host-agent progress; deferred work may remain `INITIAL_VISIT_STARTED` after callbacks drain. Both are observational; neither drives traversal. See [progress contracts](reference.md#deferred-dag-progress-and-reconciliation) and [inspection](reference.md#inspection-and-execution) for exact fields and limits.

### Carrying completion facts into a revision

Unknown `completedWork` IDs reject intentionally. Before seeding a revised definition, the host must revalidate which accepted artifacts still satisfy its task policy, then retain only IDs present in `dag.vertices` or `dag.definition.omittedIds`. Membership alone does not establish that an old result is valid for changed task data or dependencies. Keep accepted facts outside CTT; revision does not migrate them automatically. See the [revision example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-revision-example.ts).

### Observing traversal state

Use `getResolvedTreeView()` or `getResolvedGraphView()` for live queries.
Callbacks and sources receive `resolvedTreeView` or `resolvedGraphView` and
canonical `VertexHandle` / `VertexView` facets. They cannot replace CTT state or
edit its hint collections; use visitor commands for active rewrites and deletion.
Caller data, IDs, and individual hints retain shallow identity. Captured event
vertices remain historical even when their live handles change. Synthetic DAG
entry source contexts have null parent vertex/ref fields; ordinary graph and tree
parents remain visible. See [query contracts](reference.md#safe-tree-queries).

406	For heterogeneous fragments, declare the data and ID unions explicitly with `composeDag<DataA | DataB, IdA | IdB>(instances, options)`. Options cannot widen an inferred identity domain to admit foreign wire IDs. All functions and public types are exported from the root and DAG subpath. See the [runnable fragment example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-fragments-example.ts) for independent ticket-based sync/async execution.
407	
408	### Ticket coordination
409	
410	`createDagWorkSession(runner)` and `createAsyncDagWorkSession(runner)` require runners configured with `workCompletion: 'externalSettlement'`. Wrapping executes nothing and creates no additional execution owner. Callers retain direct runner access; existing single-owner rules apply.
411	
412	| Operation                                                   | Result and contract                                                                                                                                                                                       |
413	| ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
414	| `advance()`                                                 | Drains the runner, then returns `{ kind: 'awaitingSettlement', workTickets }`, `{ kind: 'paused' }`, or `{ kind: 'finished' }`. Async advance returns a promise; failures throw the exact original value. |
415	| `completeWork(ticket)`                                      | Reports accepted work completion; returns `{ kind: 'accepted' }` initially and `{ kind: 'alreadyAccepted' }` for identical replay.                                                                        |
416	| `failTraversal(ticket, error)`                              | Reports fatal traversal failure; same acceptance result union. Identical failure replay compares errors with `Object.is`; conflicting reports reject.                                                     |
417	| `summary()`                                                 | Returns the runner's detached `DagSummary<ID>` without execution or source I/O.                                                                                                                           |
418	| `getStatus()`, `getStopReason()`, `isHalted()`, `inspect()` | Shared `TraversalExecutionState` observations of the coordinated runner.                                                                                                                                  |
419	| `inspectMilestones()`                                       | Captures a detached `DagMilestoneSnapshot<ID>` for dependency explanations and queries without advancing execution.                                                                                       |
420	| `requestPause()`                                            | Returns the runner's boolean cooperative pause request result; admitted callbacks drain before pause acknowledgement.                                                                                     |
421	
422	Dispatch external work from `advance()`'s `awaitingSettlement.workTickets`, after host claim/capacity checks. `workCompleted` iterator events report committed W and cannot request dispatch; an enabled `ON_WORK_READY` visitor runs before work and can dispatch directly. Use `summary()` for progress, `inspectMilestones()` for dependency explanations, and `inspect()` for shared execution/iterator state.
423	
424	`DagWorkBoundary<ID>` discriminates the three advance results; its `workTickets` contains readonly `DagWorkTicket<ID>` objects exposing only `vertexId`. The type-only nominal ticket declaration has no runtime constructor; spreading a ticket loses its private TypeScript identity. Hidden provenance binds each ticket to its issuing facade and deferred generation. Foreign, copied, forged, and stale tickets reject before settlement mutation. Repeated observations of the same deferred work remain usable. Tickets do not transfer between two facades wrapping the same runner. The existing settlement implementation owns duplicate and conflict behavior.

426	`failTraversal(ticket, error)` is the sole fatal settlement method. Sessions expose inspection directly, including `session.inspectMilestones().explain({ vertexId, milestone: 'work' })`; snapshots do not change after later settlements.
427	
428	Observation does not advance execution, but it is not constant-cost: `inspectMilestones()` captures the current dependency graph, and summaries on lazy DAGs diagnose topology in O(V + E) while it differs from successfully validated topology. Prepared/eager runners reuse successful topology validation.
429	
430	Tickets are local capabilities with no durable serialized representation. Persist host-accepted completion facts, then call `completeWork(ticket)` and advance to observe newly eligible work. Tickets provide neither external claims nor retry/attempt policy. Fatal failure applies to the whole traversal; keep retryable work deferred under host policy.
431	
432	### Filtered DAG visitors
433	
434	`filterDagDataVisitor(predicate, callback)` and `filterAsyncDagDataVisitor(predicate, callback)` wrap ordinary DAG visitors. The synchronous predicate sees vertex **data**. A type guard narrows the callback's first argument; a boolean predicate filters without narrowing. The callback receives `(data, context)`, retaining the ordinary graph, reference, phase, group metadata, and command-result types. A false predicate invokes no callback and returns no commands. The async helper supports value-or-promise callbacks; predicate and callback errors preserve exact identity.
435	
436	```ts
437	traversal.addVisitorFor(
438	  DagVisitorPhase.ON_WORK_READY,
439	  filterDagDataVisitor(
440	    (data: Task | Group): data is Task => data.kind === 'task',
441	    (task, context) => {
442	      console.log(task.prompt, context.phase);
443	    },
444	  ),
445	);
446	```
447	
448	The host defines `Task`, `Group`, and their discriminants. The helper preserves callback ordering, command handling, and phase restrictions, including exclusive `DEFER_WORK_COMPLETION` only in `ON_WORK_READY`. Filtering alone does not defer work under `afterWorkReadyChain`; use external settlement when the host owns completion.
449	
450	### Discovery and execution as separate phases
451	
452	A DAG can be used in a **discover first, execute later** mode. Hints describe
453	how to find vertices and their structural children; dependencies describe when
454	their work is eligible. These relationships need not have the same shape.
455	
456	| Concern                  | Declared through                                                                           | Meaning                                                                                  |
457	| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
458	| Discovery and structure  | `resolveRoot()`, `resolveChild(hint)`, and `$childHints` child hints                       | Find vertices and establish structural parent/child relationships.                       |
459	| Work prerequisites       | `dependsOnWork` vertex IDs                                                                 | Hold a vertex's initial work until its prerequisites have completed their work.          |
460	| Completion prerequisites | `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion` vertex IDs                                                   | Hold initial work until the prerequisite vertices and their retained subgraphs complete. |
461	| Work completion          | Normal initial visitor-chain completion, `completedWork`, or successful guarded `settle()` | Supply the completion facts that release dependents.                                     |
462	| Subtree completion       | Structural children and the `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` lifecycle                                  | Wait for a vertex's own work and its discovered descendant subgraph to complete.         |
463	
464	For example, a synthetic root can list a flat catalog of `a`, `b`, `c`, and `d`.
465	Every real vertex can have `$childHints: []`, while `dependsOnWork` declares a diamond:
466	
467	| Vertex | Child hints (`$childHints`) | Prerequisites (`dependsOnWork`) |
468	| ------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
469	| `a`    | `[]`                        | `[]`                            |
470	| `b`    | `[]`                        | `['a']`                         |
471	| `c`    | `[]`                        | `['a']`                         |
472	| `d`    | `[]`                        | `['b', 'c']`                    |
473	
474	All four vertices are discoverable through the catalog. Initially only `a` is
475	ready; completing it releases `b` and `c`, and `d` waits for both. No child hint
476	from `a` to `b` or from `b` to `d` is needed to express these prerequisites.
477	Discovery order does not satisfy a dependency or override its readiness rule.
478	It can still influence FIFO order among equally ready vertices.
479	
480	Graph sources default to `omittedWorkDependencies: 'none'`: omitting `dependsOnWork`
481	means no work prerequisites. Set `omittedWorkDependencies: 'discoveryParentWork'` to inherit discovery-parent W
482	only for omitted lists. Explicit `dependsOnWork: []` or an ID list always wins. Children of
483	a synthetic catalog root have no implicit dependency on the catalog holder.
484	Real child hints still define structure, paths, and subtree-completion
485	obligations even when work dependencies are supplied separately.
486	
487	With `discovery: 'eager'`, the runner resolves all reachable hints and validates
488	the declared dependencies before invoking any visitor. Discovery adapters should
489	describe or fetch graph facts; put the work being scheduled in visitors or in
490	the host executor. Resolving a vertex does not itself complete its work. Internal
491	dependency bookkeeping and supplied completion seeds may be processed during
492	discovery. Default lazy mode interleaves discovery and execution instead. For a separate preview boundary, use `prepare()` as described below.
493	
494	Both DAG runners expose `prepare(): this` / `Promise<this>`. On fresh tree-source or graph-source runners without injected traversal state/containers, preparation fully discovers the closure exposed by roots, hints and prerequisite lookup and validates combined W/C constraints. It invokes no visitors, emits no execution events, commits no new real-vertex W/C and creates no deferred generations; `completedWork` seeds still supply accepted W. Empty/omitted-root previews succeed at `HALTED` / `prepared`, not FINISHED. Inspect `getResolvedGraphView()` and `summary()` before calling `run()` or iterating.
495	
496	Preparation adopts effective eager discovery even for lazy inputs, exposes that mode in summaries, and establishes eager topology freezing (hint rewrites/subtree disabling reject). Repeated preparation before execution is idempotent. Run adopts the discovered graph without repeating adapters. Preparation after execution starts, during another ownership operation, or with injected state/container objects (even empty ones) rejects recoverably. Failed preparation rethrows the exact stored error. Async preparation shares the existing owner/session: pause waits for already-admitted discovery callbacks without canceling them, then reports `paused`; another prepare continues or run adopts discovery and executes.
497	
498	For a host-controlled execution phase, combine eager discovery with a complete
499	synthetic-root catalog and `workCompletion: 'externalSettlement'`.
500	After `run()` reaches quiescence, read `summary().awaitingSettlement`; the host can execute
501	selected work and report accepted completion through guarded `settle()`, or
502	rebuild from `completedWork` on its next tick. Under the default `afterWorkReadyChain` policy, normal chain return completes W; under `externalSettlement`, even an empty or filtered chain defers. The
503	[deferred progress example below](#deferred-dag-progress-and-reconciliation)
504	implements this flat-catalog mode.
505	
506	Without `resolvePrerequisite`, a prerequisite ID does not itself discover or
507	fetch its vertex: every required vertex must be reachable through hints or
508	listed in the catalog. With that hook, the runner can request prerequisites
509	transitively before declaring them missing. Eager mode rejects unresolved
510	prerequisite IDs before visitors run. The adapter owns catalog completeness,
511	including disconnected components and cycles with no dependency-free source.
512	
513	### Discovery and completed work
514	
515	DAG graph sources accept `completedWork?: ReadonlySet<VertexId>` in both synchronous
516	and asynchronous traversal configuration. Each runner copies the set when created.
517	A listed vertex skips its initial `ON_WORK_READY` visitors and event, but its children
518	are still discovered and its `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` visit waits for their completion.
519	Omitted vertices count as recognized IDs; an ID never discovered causes a
520	`TypeError`. This option requires a fresh graph runner and cannot be combined
521	with a tree source or injected continuation state/container.
522	
523	Set `discovery: 'eager'` to resolve every reachable hint before the first visitor,
524	including descendants of vertices whose work dependencies are still blocked.
525	The runner then validates the original declared dependencies for missing IDs and
526	cycles, even when `completedWork` has already satisfied those dependencies.
527	Unknown seed IDs also fail before visitors in eager mode. Seeded lazy runners
528	validate original dependencies when discovery closes; ordinary lazy traversal
529	remains the default. Eager discovery honors explicit root `dependsOnWork` entries.
530	`priority` result metadata rejects with `TypeError('priority metadata is not supported')`.
531	
532	Ordinary roots honor declared W and C prerequisites in lazy/eager mode, with or
533	without seeds or lookup. `rootWorkDependencies: 'honor'` is the default. Explicit
534	`rootWorkDependencies: 'ignore'` restores ignoring root W only; root C still applies.
535	Synthetic catalog roots are bookkeeping and have no work dependencies.
536	
537	Without `resolvePrerequisite`, a prerequisite must be discovered or deliberately
538	omitted. Omission satisfies W and C; deletion cascades through both
539	kinds of dependent. Completed-work seeds satisfy only W, so a seeded composite
540	still completes its children and completion callback before releasing C gates.
541	Original W/C declarations are validated even when W was seeded. Lazy discovery
542	retains its existing admission order and reports known invalid stalls; eager
543	discovery validates the full reachable topology before visitors.
544	
545	Progress `unmetPrerequisiteIds` is the stable union of unsatisfied W and C gates.
546	Vertices with a nonempty completion declaration also expose
547	`unmetSubgraphPrerequisiteIds`, which becomes `[]` when satisfied. Graph vertices
548	expose a copied `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion` only when its normalized list is nonempty.
549	See the runnable [build-join example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-completion-dependencies-example.ts).
550	
551	Graph sources may define `resolvePrerequisite(id)` to find an unknown ID declared
552	in either prerequisite list. It returns a tagged `found`, `omitted`, or `missing` result (or a promise-like result
553	for `AsyncDagTraversal`), with exactly the ID as its argument and no fabricated
554	parent context. A default-unknown result with no `vertexId` field inherits the requested ID; typed live results must supply an own ID, and inherited fields reject.
555	An explicit ID must match using SameValueZero identity. `{ kind: 'missing' }` means not found and eventually produces the typed
556	missing-prerequisite stall. `{ kind: 'omitted', satisfiesDependencies: true }`
557	deliberately omits the requested ID and satisfies both W and C. A `found`
558	result wraps the non-null content and optional declarations under `vertex`.
559	Deprecated lookup `undefined` and `{ vertexContent: null }` inputs still normalize
560	to missing and omission respectively.
561	Thrown/rejected values pass through unchanged. First-accepted identity wins when
562	lookup and ordinary discovery race: a live vertex retains its original content
563	and declarations, including when a later result deliberately omits it. If omission was
564	accepted first, later content rejects with the existing omission/content error.
565	
566	Lookup prefers available ordinary discovery. Eager traversal alternates natural
567	discovery and lookup until both reach closure, then validates before visitors.
568	Lazy traversal looks up unknown declarations when available work/discovery has
569	been consumed; it preserves lazy expansion for known blocked vertices. Found
570	vertices can declare further prerequisites. Shared W/C demand coalesces to one
571	outstanding callback per ID. Not-found answers are cached for that runner;
572	later ordinary discovery can still supply the vertex. Unused `completedWork`
573	IDs are never fetched. All callbacks share the configured concurrency limit.
574	
575	A found prerequisite is a real detached component: no invented discovery edge,
576	parent, or child slot, and public depth zero even with a synthetic root. It has
577	an independent anchor that survives removal of a later discovery parent. Its
578	normal children follow ordinary pruning; explicitly deleting the anchor or the
579	ordinary traversal root still deletes it. The runner finishes only after all
580	retained components finish. Structural graph views include these components
581	without adding dependency edges, so callers displaying a graph should enumerate
582	`getVertexRefs()` instead of assuming everything is reachable from `getRoot()`.
583	
584	Deleting all consumers invalidates a queued lookup and ignores an already-started
585	outcome. Accepted anchors remain retained even when their consumers finish or
586	are deleted. Halting starts no new lookups; outcomes received while halted are
587	stored and applied on resume. Summaries and inspection do not invoke callbacks
588	or consume outcomes, and discovery remains partial while lookup is pending.
589	A live runner owns pending lookup handles; they cannot be transferred through
590	the data-only continuation seed. A new runner may repeat lookups. Lookup handles
591	remain runner-local and nonpersistent. Durable caching and persistence of graph
592	and accepted completion facts belong to the host.
593	See the executable [module-registry lookup example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-prerequisite-resolution-example.ts).
594	
595	Set `syntheticRoot: true` when `resolveRoot()` returns a catalog holder whose child
596	hints describe multiple graph sources. Its supplied ID is ignored in favor of a
597	private identity, and its children have no implicit dependency on it. Every
598	catalog entry needs an explicit ID from the hint identity callback or the vertex
599	result. Repeating an ID within the catalog is an error; shared descendants under
600	real vertices remain valid. Combine this option with eager discovery to validate
601	a complete catalog, including disconnected components, before work begins. The
602	adapter is responsible for listing its entire domain.
603	
604	Synthetic roots produce no visitor calls or events. `getResolvedGraphView()`, visitor
605	and resolver graph views, and retained original views omit the synthetic vertex and its
606	edges. Their `getRoot()` returns `null`; paths follow only real parent edges.
607	Explicit catalog membership retains a listed vertex even after its sole real parent is deleted.
608	`noRoot` is therefore a no-op, while `noSelf` still removes the target vertex.
609	An empty catalog finishes without events. The runner's internal graph container
610	retains the synthetic vertex for scheduling.
611	
612	Enabled eager/synthetic options require a fresh graph-source runner. Explicit
613	`discovery: 'lazy'` and `syntheticRoot: false` remain compatible with tree sources.
614	Eager mode rejects child-hint rewrites and subtree-disabling commands after
615	validation; data rewrites and vertex deletion retain their existing behavior.

617	### Structural sinks
618	
619	`hasSingleStructuralSink(graph)` counts vertices with no **structural children** in a resolved graph view. It returns true only when exactly one such vertex exists: an empty graph returns false, and a single isolated leaf returns true. Work and completion dependency arrows do not affect this count; use `inspectMilestones()` for milestone dependency questions.
620	
621	### DAG dependency queries and explanations
622	
623	`runner.inspectMilestones()` and the equivalent free function `inspectDagMilestones(runner)` capture a synchronous detached `DagMilestoneSnapshot<ID>` from either sync or async DAG runner (no `await` needed), including tree-source runners with their existing unknown ID domain. Import it and `DagExplanation`, `DagBlocker`, `DagMilestoneStatus`, `DagMilestoneQueryOptions`, and `DagMilestoneQueryResult` from the package root or DAG subpath. Capture performs no callbacks, source lookup, scheduling, settlement, or iterator ownership changes. Methods reuse that capture after the runner advances; take another inspection for current facts. Owned arrays and result records are copied on every query. IDs and caller data retain shallow identity and are never frozen.
624	
625	After a DAG runner finishes or fails, `inspectMilestones()` and `summary()` on that existing runner remain observational reads of its retained committed W/C, partial discovery, and progress facts. They perform no source I/O, resume no execution, and do not turn failure into successful work. Query arrays and result records remain detached, with shallow ID/data identity; a captured milestone snapshot does not refresh itself. A failed runner retains its exact original thrown or rejected value, including `null` or `undefined`, and inspection does not clear that failure. There is no public state-restoration constructor or raw-container injection route. To reconstruct an execution, create a fresh runner or session from a source or prepared definition and supply host-accepted `completedWork` facts.
626	
627	Milestone targets are structural inputs: class getters and non-enumerable `vertexId`/`milestone` fields are supported. Each field is read once into an owned target record; getter-thrown values propagate unchanged.
628	
629	Call `prerequisitesOf({ vertexId, milestone: 'work' | 'subgraphCompletion' }, { transitive?: boolean })` or `dependentsOf(...)`. Both return `{ milestones, edges, discoveryComplete }`, defaulting to direct constraints. Transitive queries use deterministic breadth-first order, preserve discovery/declaration order, deduplicate by SameValueZero ID and milestone, and exclude the starting milestone from the milestone list. Original edges retain **waiter waits for prerequisite** direction even for dependent queries, with reasons `workDependency`, `subgraphCompletionDependency`, `ownWork`, and `structuralChild`. They remain visible after satisfaction. Cycles terminate and retain returning edges. Unknown targets return empty navigation, including unresolved IDs appearing only as edge destinations. Hidden roots holders never appear.
630	
631	`explain(target)` distinguishes three results:
632	
633	| `kind`    | Fields and meaning                                                                                                                                                                                |
634	| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
635	| `unknown` | `target`, `discoveryComplete`; identity is not known in this capture                                                                                                                              |
636	| `deleted` | `target`, `discoveryComplete`; a known tombstone, never successful work                                                                                                                           |
637	| `known`   | `target`, `satisfied`, `progress`, `blockers`, `discoveryComplete`; live progress is a detached `DagVertexProgress<ID>`, while known omissions have null progress, satisfied true and no blockers |
638	
639	Live W is satisfied only after work commits (including accepted seeds); live C requires its own committed completion transition. A seed for a parent therefore does not satisfy C while retained children remain incomplete. Ready/deferred W remains unsatisfied. Readiness describes dependency eligibility and never proves a host claim, dispatch, or business outcome.
640	
641	`blockers` is a flat causal graph. Constraint records come first in breadth-first order; terminal facts then follow visited-milestone order. Only unmet original constraints reachable from the target appear, and traversal stops at satisfied milestones. The `DagBlocker<ID>` tagged union is:
642	
643	| `kind`              | Fields and meaning                                                                                                                     |
644	| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
645	| `constraint`        | Original `waiter`, `prerequisite`, `reason`, plus `waiterStatus` and `prerequisiteStatus`                                              |
646	| `unfinishedWork`    | Work `target` and `work: 'pending' \| 'ready' \| 'visiting' \| 'deferred'`; a reachable unfinished W with no unmet outgoing constraint |
647	| `discoveryOpen`     | Completion `target`; this vertex's expansion is unprepared/open, so retained children are not yet fully known                          |
648	| `completionPending` | Completion `target`; W and retained children are complete and expansion is closed, but C has not committed                             |
649	
650	Endpoint status is `{ kind: 'live', work: DagWorkState, satisfied: boolean }` or `{ kind: 'omitted' | 'deleted' | 'unresolved' }`. Thus an unsatisfied C endpoint can explicitly have `work: 'completed', satisfied: false`. Omitted endpoints satisfy their milestones and do not appear as blockers. Unresolved endpoints are unknown identities, even when global discovery is complete; during partial discovery they are not proof of a missing source vertex. `discoveryOpen` uses local expansion state, independently of global `discoveryComplete`. A closed leaf does not acquire that blocker because another lookup is pending.
651	
652	Engine-produced `DagVertexProgress` includes exact `unmetWorkPrerequisiteIds`, independent of `unmetSubgraphPrerequisiteIds`; the existing `unmetPrerequisiteIds` remains their union. Both W and C fields are required readonly arrays, including when empty; manually constructed records must supply both. Do not recover W by subtracting C from the union when the same ID participates in both.
653	
654	See the runnable [DAG inspection example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-inspection-example.ts).

656	### Deferred DAG progress and reconciliation
657	
658	Set `workCompletion: 'externalSettlement'` to inspect
659	candidates without completing their work. Enabled callbacks and their commands finish before normal deferral, including when there are no callbacks. Both DAG runners expose `summary()` and
660	`settle(id, outcome, expectedGeneration)`. Import `DagSummary`,
661	`DagVertexProgress`, `DagDeferredWork`, `DagWorkState`, `DagSettlementGeneration`, and
662	`DagSettlementOutcome` from the package root or DAG subpath.
663	
664	<!-- standalone -->
665	
666	```ts
667	import { DagTraversal, type VertexTypes } from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
668	
669	type Graph = VertexTypes<string, string>;
670	const prerequisites: Record<string, string[]> = {
671	  a: [],
672	  b: ['a'],
673	  c: ['a'],
674	  d: ['b', 'c'],
675	};
676	// In-memory stand-in for accepted completion facts loaded from host storage.
677	const acceptedCompletedWork = new Set(['a']);
678	const traversal = new DagTraversal<Graph>({
679	  workCompletion: 'externalSettlement',
680	  completedWork: acceptedCompletedWork,
681	  discovery: 'eager',
682	  syntheticRoot: true,
683	  traversableGraph: {
684	    resolveRoot: () => ({
685	      kind: 'found' as const,
686	      vertex: {
687	        vertexContent: { $data: '', $childHints: Object.keys(prerequisites) },
688	      },
689	    }),
690	    resolveChild: (id) => ({
691	      kind: 'found' as const,
692	      vertex: {
693	        vertexId: id,
694	        dependsOnWork: prerequisites[id]!,
695	        vertexContent: { $data: id, $childHints: [] },
696	      },
697	    }),
698	  },
699	});
700	const runner = traversal.createRunner().run(); // HALTED, waiting for the host
701	const snapshot = runner.summary();
702	console.log(snapshot.readyOrDeferredIds); // ['b', 'c']
703	const work = snapshot.awaitingSettlement.find(
704	  ({ vertexId }) => vertexId === 'b',
705	)!;
706	
707	// A real host validates and durably accepts its result before settlement.
708	acceptedCompletedWork.add('b');
709	runner.settle(work.vertexId, { kind: 'workCompleted' }, work.generation);
710	runner.run();
711	console.log(runner.summary().readyOrDeferredIds); // ['c']; d still waits for c
712	```
713	
714	Dispatch external work from `summary().awaitingSettlement`, whose `DagDeferredWork<ID>` records atomically contain readonly `{ vertexId, generation }`. Each snapshot lists exactly live deferred vertices without an accepted outcome, in discovery order, excluding queued-only, settled and deleted work. Arrays/records are detached and opaque ID objects retain identity; the snapshot does not claim host work. `readyOrDeferredIds` includes ready and deferred work, excluding visiting and completed work.
715	
716	DAG iterator events use `DagEvent<T, ID = unknown>` with required `vertexId: ID`, preserving sync/async runner identity inference. Its discriminants are `kind: 'workCompleted'` for committed W and `kind: 'subgraphCompleted'` for committed C. These events have no callback `phase` or legacy `order` field. `emitEvents` selects committed kinds, while `visitorPhases` selects `DagVisitorPhase.ON_WORK_READY` and `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` callbacks. Commit timing and event ordering are unchanged. ON_WORK_READY visitor callbacks remain pre-work. Seeded W emits no synthetic work event. Deferred `workCompleted` events emit only on successful settlement, not when dispatch becomes possible. A real `ON_WORK_READY` callback can instead dispatch before its chain defers. Synthetic roots and `completedWork` seeds do not need new settlement. `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` remains automatic after W, discovery, children, and completion prerequisites are satisfied.
717	
718	The explicit `DEFER_WORK_COMPLETION` command ends the initial visitor chain early, discards its uncommitted buffered
719	commands, and skips remaining visitors. It emits no event or dependency success
720	and holds no physical callback permit. Already committed changes and external
721	visitor effects cannot be undone. Deferral is rejected in completion and tree callbacks. It must be the only
722	command in its result: mixed batches reject before any commands apply. The
723	retired `DEFER_READY` exported symbol is removed. Deferred vertices may expand their own hints in lazy
724	mode; use eager discovery and a complete synthetic-root catalog for a global
725	frontier, including descendants of deferred parents.
726	
727	`summary()` invokes no callbacks or resolvers and does not advance scheduling. It reports progress; `inspectMilestones()` captures dependency constraints/blockers, while `inspect()` reports execution and iterator state.
728	Its detached map, entries and arrays have readonly TypeScript types and retain
729	original ID identity without freezing caller objects. It reports discovery mode/completeness, per-vertex work
730	state and unmet prerequisites. `DagVertexProgress.vertexId` preserves caller identity;
731	`work: 'visiting'` means a visitor chain is active. `subgraphComplete` reports C,
732	and both `unmetWorkPrerequisiteIds` and `unmetSubgraphPrerequisiteIds` are required readonly arrays reporting exact unsatisfied W and C prerequisites, including empty arrays. The same ID may occur in both; `unmetPrerequisiteIds` is their deduplicated union, so subtracting C from that union cannot recover W.
733	`completedWorkIds` and `completedSubgraphIds` report committed W and C.
734	`readyOrDeferredIds` includes ready and deferred work, excluding visiting and completed
735	work. `deferredWorkIds` includes all deferred work, retaining accepted outcomes while W is uncommitted;
736	`awaitingSettlement` contains only deferred work still awaiting an outcome, as detached
737	`{ vertexId, generation }` records. Successful settlement commits W immediately;
738	accepted traversal failure removes dispatch eligibility while leaving W uncommitted.
739	`activeVisitorVertexIds` includes active visitor chains, including completion chains
740	whose W is already committed. Counts `readyOrDeferred`, `deferredWork`,
741	`activeVisitorVertices`, `workCompleted` and `subgraphCompleted` match those collections
742	and overlap rather than partition vertices. These are runner callbacks,
743	not external host attempts. `unusedCompletedWorkIds` exposes unrecognized seeds;
744	`diagnostics` describes known invalid graph structure, never deferred blockers
745	alone. Before root discovery, completeness is false. Lazy partial snapshots do
746	not promise a complete global frontier. Synthetic bookkeeping is absent.
